newsitem.title: EGYPT: Banks, mills put Cairo stocks at two-week low.
newsitem.headline: Banks, mills put Cairo stocks at two-week low.

text.p: Blue-chip banking and milling stocks stumbled slightly on Monday and helped send the Cairo bourse all-share price index to a two-week low.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) index slipped 0.15 points to 347.84 points, it lowest level since the beginning of the month. Volume was an average 41.81 million pounds ($12.32 million).
"All the indicators needed to send the market higher are in place but the market is just not reacting," said Tarek Lotfy, an insitutional broker at Intercaptial Securities.

"I'm confident about the outlook. The market needs to trade up, it has to, but when that will happen nobody knows. So investors are either waiting or quietly building their positions. Some are getting out," he added.
Lofty said skittish investors disappointed at the market were perpetuating the downtrend by selling their shares.
He said traders unhappy with the performance of the popular milling sector had driven prices down further, even affecting recent privatisation Alexandria Flour Mills.

The state sold Alexandria Flour Mills more than a week ago at 82.5 pounds per share and on Monday it shed 0.01 to 79.99 pounds. Central and West Delta Flour Mills also fell 1.08 to 79.98 pounds while Upper Egypt Flour Mills edged 0.3 pounds lower to 74.99.
General Silos and Storage, which usually tracks the mills, also fell 0.5 to 87.5 pounds.
Egyptian American Bank, in which the state sold 319,300 shares through the exchange on Sunday, was the day's most active share with over six million pounds traded but it fell 0.65 to 120 pounds.
The state had offered investors 1.2 million shares at 127 pounds each and one of the agents for the sale said most investors wanted to buy the stock at around 110 to 112.
"It was too expensive so the stock will fall. The prices are coming off now so investors are setting in," Lotfy said.
In the same sector, Commercial International Bank eased 0.5 to 72 pounds in four million pounds of trade while other banks were barely changed in small turnover.
The popular cement sector saw quiet trading but prices closed slightly firmer. Helwan Cement, the most active share in the sector, rose 0.93 to 70.
Institutional buying helped boost turnover in Nile Cotton Ginning and Eipico/Egyptian International Pharmaceutical Industries but both stocks ended unchanged at 53 pounds and 220 pounds respectively.
Genuine demand for Heliopolis Housing and Development helped push prices 5.5 pounds higher to 418 but Lotfy said there was no reason behind the sudden investor interest.
"There has been no news on the company, nothing. It's inexplicable," he added.
The index for openly traded firms rose to 475.33 points from 475.18 points on Sunday and that for the rarely traded "closed" firms fell to 257.54 from 257.74 points.
Of the 89 shares traded, 31 rose, 40 fell while 18 ended unchanged, the CMA said.
$1 = 3.395 pounds
